STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0, u1
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach) -> u2
(u0, zombie_killed & !top_breach) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, top_breach) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, top_breach, u2) -> -10
(u0, zombie_killed & !top_breach, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, top_breach, u2) -> -10

The only violation event is top_breach, which moves u0 or u1 to the non-accepting absorbing u2 with -10; success at the 300-step cut equals ending in u0/u1, matching the environment success flag (true exactly while no top breach has occurred). Since one top breach permanently fails the task, the absence of any edge out of u2 is the correct treatment and no regression edges are required. FINAL_STATES is present, nonempty, and its members u0 and u1 are declared and both accepting (both mean 'no top breach yet'), with u2 correctly excluded; u0 being initial-and-final is right for a safety task. Reachability: u0 is initial, u1 is reached by any first kill, u2 by a breach; u1 will occur in virtually every successful episode because killing is the only way to stop a top-lane zombie, so no unreachable state exists. Guards use only the four defined event propositions, with no invented predicates. Ordered coverage is sound: per-state guard lists are disjoint (top_breach and zombie_killed can never co-occur, so the !top_breach conjunct in the u0 kill guard is redundant but harmless), else is listed last, and the task-irrelevant side_breach and plant_trampled are absorbed by the per-state else self-loops in u0 and u1; u2's sole else self-loop keeps it properly absorbing for later breaches, tramples, and kills. Reward safety: no cycle pays reward — the +0.1 can be paid at most once (u0->u1) and the -10 at most once (from whichever of u0/u1 is current), so cumulative reward is bounded in [-10, +0.1]; unpunished repeat breaches inside u2 are acceptable because the episode outcome is already fixed by the first breach. Minor non-blocking notes: the kill bonus is a bounded but sparse nudge (paid only on the first kill) rather than dense progress reward; a per-kill self-loop was sensibly avoided since the propositions cannot distinguish top-lane from side-lane kills and a per-kill bonus would reward chasing side-lane zombies instead of guarding. Format matches the paper template (STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES headers, (s, guard) -> s' transitions, (s, guard, s') -> r reward lines with guards matching the transition function exactly).
